questions.q: Which two generic tests does this lesson attach to the customer_id column, turning Lesson 1's 'trustworthy' into something checkable?
options: not_null and unique
accepted_values and relationships
primary_key and foreign_key
min_value and max_value
questions.explain: not_null ensures every row has a customer_id, and unique ensures no customer_id value repeats — together, exactly the concrete definition of 'trust' from Lesson 1.

questions.q: What does the not_null test on customer_id roughly compile down to?
options: A select statement that returns rows where customer_id is null; any returned rows mean the test fails
A command that deletes rows with a null customer_id
A Snowflake constraint that physically blocks null values from being inserted
A Python script that counts null values and emails the result
questions.explain: Every generic dbt test compiles to a select statement that should return zero rows; for not_null, that's a select of rows where the column is null.

questions.q: Where does this lesson's schema.yml file live, and why there?
options: Next to the staging model's .sql file, in models/staging/jaffle_shop/, following the same pairing the prerequisite dbt course taught
Inside profiles.yml, alongside the Snowflake connection
In a top-level tests/ folder, separate from any model
Inside raw_customers.csv, as a header comment
questions.explain: The schema.yml file sits next to stg_jaffle_shop__customers.sql, using the same data_tests: key and pairing of descriptions with tests from the dbt course.

questions.q: What command runs just the tests attached to the staging model, without testing the rest of the project?
options: dbt test --select stg_jaffle_shop__customers
dbt run --select stg_jaffle_shop__customers
dbt debug --select stg_jaffle_shop__customers
dbt init --select stg_jaffle_shop__customers
questions.explain: dbt test --select <model> runs only that model's attached tests, the same scoped pattern as dbt run --select used in Lesson 6.

questions.q: If a duplicate customer_id value existed in the real data, what's the honest next step, according to this lesson?
options: Query the staging model directly to find the actual failing row and investigate why the raw data has a duplicate
Delete the unique test so the project passes again
Rename the column to avoid the conflict
Ignore the FAIL line since it doesn't block dbt run
questions.explain: The lesson explicitly says the honest move is to investigate the real failing row, not delete the test — the same troubleshooting habit taught in the prerequisite dbt course.
